subject: Technical deep-dive recap: latency/throughput SLOs and deployment topology
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit@finexco.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Technical deep-dive recap: latency/throughput SLOs and deployment topology

Hi Amit —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Recap below from our call and the next steps we discussed. Please let me know if I missed anything.

Key pain points you described:
- High tail latency on your current in-house transformer endpoints during peak billing hours (p95 spikes to ~1.2s).
- Unpredictable throughput when new user cohorts are routed to heavy-context prompts (3–4x token lengths).
- Need for private network deployment and control plane separation (data residency + SOC2 requirements).

Goals you shared:
- p95 generation latency <= 200ms for short-context requests (<=256 tokens).
- p99 latency target <= 500ms across typical user distributions.
- Support sustained 120 requests/sec at 1k token average with ability to burst to 300rps.
- Model: ~13B open model family with streaming and function/tool calling.
- VPC-onboarding and dedicated capacity for initial rollout; evaluate Private deployment for regulated workloads.

Technical notes from our discussion:
- Suggested topology: Redwood Dedicated pool (reserved capacity) in us-west-2 with optional Private control plane behind your VPC. Dedicated shards sized to handle 120 rps; autoscale policy to add warm shards on sustained 10%+ over baseline.
- KV-cache and prefix caching will be configured to reduce repeat-token cost for conversational flows.
- Quantization recommendation: start with 4-bit quantized variant for the 13B model to balance GPU memory and single-token latency; we can recommend specific kernels after we validate sequence-length distribution.
- Networking: we will need your egress IP CIDR ranges and SAML SSO metadata; procurement asked for the network diagram — attached.

Open questions / clarifications we need from you:
1) Typical input token distribution (p50/p90/p99) across the most common endpoints — helps us size KV cache and batch window.
2) Any hard SLA date for production cutover and initial traffic % for canary.
3) Procurement contact and billing PO timing.

Next steps (agreed):
- I will share a short SLO proposal and pricing estimate (attached: redwood-slo-proposal.pdf).
- Aditya and Neha will follow up with a proposed capacity plan and kernel/quantization options.
- Schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra (+network) team: proposed slots Wed 2027-06-10 10:00–11:00 PT or Thu 2027-06-11 08:00–09:00 PT. Please confirm.

Attachments: redwood-slo-proposal.pdf, finexco-network-diagram.png

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0199

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 07:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Technical deep-dive recap: latency/throughput SLOs and deployment topology

Hi Amit — quick follow-up with the technical bits we flagged on the call.

Sizing and perf assumptions we used for the estimate: 
- Baseline request profile: avg 1k tokens in / 1.2k tokens out (you confirmed average ~1k).
- Target sustained throughput: 120 rps -> we modeled this as 4 shards of our Dedicated pool (NVIDIA A10G-equivalent) with concurrent stream slots tuned for low-latency tails.
- Batching policy: dynamic batching with 8–12 ms batch windows for short requests, larger windows for long-form generation; works with KV cache to avoid repeated prefix compute.
- Latency expectations: with the above config and 4-bit quantized 13B runtimes we expect p95 <= 200ms for <=256 token contexts; p99 under 500ms for the majority of requests, assuming network RTTs <25ms from your region to us-west-2.

On model compatibility and fallbacks:
- Streaming support and tool-calling: supported via our streaming API; end-to-end traceability (token-level) will be available in Console.
- Fallback model variants: recommend a smaller 7B variant for extremely latency-sensitive endpoints and a 13B quantized variant for quality-sensitive flows. Auto-fallback routing is possible by route.

Network & security checklist (need from FinexCo):
- VPC peering details or egress IP CIDR list for firewall allowlist.
- SAML metadata (IdP) and primary SSO admin contact.
- Contact for SOC2 evidence requests if they want to accelerate compliance review.

I'll attach a technical capacity plan in the next email (PDF) and include kernel/quantization matrix once we run sequence-length samples. If you can send a 48-hour sample of request telemetry (anonymized), we can produce exact estimates.

Aditya
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime
aditya@redwood.com
